---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Funding Autonomy With Revealed Distribution
EXPRESSION: MIN(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(MA(oancf, 3), dlc), ADD(ABS(MA(oancf, 3)), ADD(dlc, 1))), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(prstkc, dvt), ADD(sstk, dltis)), at), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Capital returned to shareholders is credible evidence of underpriced cash generation only when the firm is not simultaneously obliged to the credit market; a distribution from a firm whose maturing debt exceeds its operating cash flow is a transfer from creditors, whereas a distribution from a firm with funding autonomy is genuine surplus.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The archive shows a sharp split — coverage-type signals produce reliable FF5 alpha (5.2% at t=3.68) while net-payout constructs produce strong Fama-MacBeth slopes but almost no alpha — and the natural diagnosis is that unconditional payout is spanned by RMW/CMA while payout backed by funding autonomy is not. MIN enforces the conjunction so a firm cannot enter the long leg on coverage alone or payout alone, which directly tests whether the payout theme adds anything once the funding-obligation state is controlled.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Total Debt Repayment Capacity
EXPRESSION: RATIO(MA(oancf, 3), ADD(ADD(dltt, dlc), ABS(MA(oancf, 3))))
HYPOTHESIS: If the winning coverage mechanism reflects genuine solvency rather than a near-term liquidity calendar, then normalized operating cash flow measured against the *entire* debt stock should predict returns at least as well as against current maturities alone, because it measures how many years of internal cash would extinguish all creditor claims.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This isolates one specific design choice in the archive's best family — the scope of the obligation (short-dated only versus total debt) — which determines whether future refinements should target rollover timing or overall creditor burden. The bounded [-1, 1] form treats cash-burning firms correctly and, because dltt and dlc are balance-sheet items reported by nearly all firms, coverage should be comparable to or better than the parent's 0.091.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Volatile Cash Flow With Short Dated Debt
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(VOL(RATIO(oancf, at), 5)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, at), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Funding risk is a mismatch problem: short-maturity debt is dangerous in proportion to how uncertain the cash flow that must service it is, so firms combining volatile operating cash generation with heavy near-term obligations face refinancing exactly when their results disappoint, and they underperform stable firms with identical average coverage.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The gen-3 stress-coverage result (alpha 4.6%, t=3.09) hinted that the tail of cash flow matters, but it fused the tail and the obligation into one ratio; this separates them so the second moment of profitability is the conditioning variable and near-term debt is the exposure. It is the only signal in the batch whose profitability leg is a risk measure rather than a level, so it discriminates a risk-mismatch mechanism from a simple cash-rich/debt-light quality tilt.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Rising Cost Of Debt Despite Operating Profits
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(MA(RATIO(oiadp, at), 3)), NEG(ZSCORE(WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(xint, ADD(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1)), 1), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Interest expense per dollar of debt is the price creditors charge the firm; when that implied rate rises for a firm that still reports healthy operating profitability, informed lenders are repricing risk that the equity market has not yet recognized, while a falling implied rate for a profitable firm signals improving creditworthiness that will later show up in equity valuation.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: No archive signal has used the price of capital — only its quantity — so this tests whether credit-market pricing information leads equity returns, a genuinely different channel from coverage or payout. The financing leg is a centered change in a rate, so it is orthogonal to the level of leverage and to asset growth, and oiadp, xint, dltt and dlc are all widely reported, giving coverage in the 0.12 range achieved by the gen-3 interest-burden signal.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Persistent Coverage Of Near Term Obligations
EXPRESSION: MUL(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(SUB(oancf, dlc), 0), 5), RANK(RATIO(SUB(MA(oancf, 3), dlc), ADD(ABS(MA(oancf, 3)), ADD(dlc, 1)))))
HYPOTHESIS: A firm that has covered its near-term debt out of operating cash in every one of the last five years has demonstrated structural funding independence, whereas a firm that covers today but failed twice recently is a cyclical borrower whose current coverage will not survive the next downturn; the market prices the current state and underweights the track record.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The archive's coverage family has been tested only as a current level, a tail, and a change, never as a frequency, and the frequency statistic captures a different economic property — reliability of the funding position across states of the world. Multiplying the 0-5 count by the continuous current-coverage rank supplies a within-bucket tiebreaker, avoiding the lumpy decile boundaries that plausibly produced the perverse Sharpe of the gen-0 count construct and the null gen-1 signed count.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Internally Funded Debt Retirement
EXPRESSION: MIN(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(dltr, dltis), at), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: The clearest evidence of underpriced cash generation on the debt side is a firm that both produces strong operating cash and uses it to retire more debt than it raises; such firms shrink creditor claims on future cash flow without any market transaction, whereas cash-generative firms that keep rolling debt forward are recycling rather than earning.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The theme's "return capital" idea has been tested almost entirely through the equity channel (buybacks, dividends, share issuance); this is its debt-channel counterpart, and paired with Signal 1 it tells us whether conditioned capital return works through repaying creditors, through paying shareholders, or both. Using dltr as a *use of internal cash* rather than as a proxy for scheduled maturities repairs the gen-2 misuse of that variable that the critic correctly identified.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---CRITIQUE Funding Autonomy With Revealed Distribution---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: A defensible conjunction that swaps the cash-flow-level leg of the archive's gen-2 MIN construct for the stronger short-debt coverage leg, so it is incremental rather than novel, but the "distribution is only credible absent creditor claims" gating is economically coherent and directly tests whether the payout theme survives conditioning on funding autonomy.

---CRITIQUE Total Debt Repayment Capacity---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This is operating-cash-flow-to-total-debt, a standard credit-quality ratio close to published cash-flow-to-debt/leverage-quality measures, and relative to the archive it is essentially a denominator swap on the existing coverage signal (and largely spanned by the gen-3 debt-service-capacity ratio), so it is a cosmetic ablation rather than a substantive mechanism test.

---CRITIQUE Volatile Cash Flow With Short Dated Debt---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: The construction is internally inconsistent with the hypothesis — because RANK(VOL) is non-negative, the sign is set entirely by the dlc z-score and the magnitude by volatility, so the long (most negative) leg is populated by *high*-volatility firms with low short debt while the "stable" firms the hypothesis wants to reward sit near zero in the middle, and the volatility leg additionally risks rediscovering the known cash-flow/earnings-volatility anomaly.

---CRITIQUE Rising Cost Of Debt Despite Operating Profits---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 4
RATIONALE: Using the implied interest rate (xint per dollar of debt) as a credit-market *price* signal is a genuinely new channel relative to the archive's quantity-based coverage and issuance measures, and the change-in-rate form is plausibly orthogonal to leverage level, though the implementation is exposed to mechanical distortion when debt is issued or retired mid-year and to common macro rate movements that will not cross-sectionally differentiate.

---CRITIQUE Persistent Coverage Of Near Term Obligations---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: A frequency-of-coverage statistic is a legitimately different property from the level, tail, and change forms already tested in the coverage family, but the archive's two prior count constructs both failed and the 0–5 integer count will still dominate the [0,1] rank tiebreaker, so the lumpy-portfolio concern the proposal claims to fix is only partially addressed.

---CRITIQUE Internally Funded Debt Retirement---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The debt-channel counterpart to the payout theme is a reasonable and previously untested conjunction, but the second leg is net debt issuance with the sign reversed, which is close to the well-documented net-external-financing/debt-issuance anomaly and partly overlaps the gen-2 pecking-order signal, so any result will need to be shown incremental to plain net debt issuance.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Creditor Claims Outgrowing Cash Generation
EXPRESSION: RATIO(SUB(DELTA(MA(oancf, 3), 1), DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1)), ADD(ABS(DELTA(MA(oancf, 3), 1)), ADD(ABS(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Solvency is a race between two flows: the cash the business generates and the creditor claims stacked against it; a firm whose normalized operating cash flow is growing faster than its debt stock is widening its funding cushion regardless of where the level sits, while a firm adding debt faster than cash flow is consuming cushion and will eventually have to finance on the market's terms.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio
REASONING: Rather than swapping the denominator of the archive's level-coverage ratio, this changes the object being measured from a stock position to the relative growth rates of the two competing flows, so it is informative even for firms whose current coverage is unremarkable and it is not spanned by the gen-3 debt-service-capacity level. The symmetric bounded form keeps the measure scale-free and comparable across firm sizes, and it treats a firm that shrinks debt while cash flow falls differently from one that grows both.
REASONING: Inputs (oancf, dltt, dlc) are widely reported, so coverage should be at least as high as the 0.09-0.13 range of the coverage family.

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Downside Adjusted Coverage Of Near Term Debt
EXPRESSION: RATIO(SUB(SUB(MA(oancf, 3), VOL(oancf, 5)), dlc), ADD(ABS(MA(oancf, 3)), ADD(dlc, 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: The relevant question is whether the firm can cover its maturing debt in a bad draw of its own cash-flow distribution, so the correct comparison is normal-year operating cash flow marked down by one standard deviation of its own volatility against near-term obligations; firms that still clear this bar are immune to refinancing pressure, and firms that fail it are exposed precisely when their results disappoint.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: This repairs the sign inconsistency the critic identified — volatility now unambiguously reduces the score and near-term debt unambiguously reduces it, so the long leg is stable cash generators with light maturities and the short leg is volatile firms with heavy maturities, exactly as the hypothesis states. It is also distinct from the gen-3 empirical-minimum version: a parametric one-sigma markdown uses the whole distribution of cash flow rather than a single realized worst year, so it separates firms whose bad year was a one-off from those with chronically unstable cash generation.
REASONING: Because volatility enters as a level subtraction rather than as a separate ranked leg, the construct cannot degenerate into the standalone cash-flow-volatility anomaly; the volatility term only matters relative to the size of the maturing debt it must cushion.
